title: Energy Transformations
seo_title: Grade 10 Science: Energy Transformations Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Energy is conserved: potential and kinetic energy, the law of conservation of energy, work, power and efficiency, and energy transformations in BC's energy systems. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 10, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 science worksheets (BC): kinetic and potential energy, work, conservation of energy, power and efficiency. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy is never created or destroyed.
body_html:
How to think about it

Gravitational potential energy is PE = mgh (g = 9.8 N/kg) and kinetic energy is KE = ½mv². As a ball falls, PE changes into KE, and the total stays the same if no energy is lost to friction or air resistance.

Work is energy transferred by a force: W = Fd. Power is the rate of transfer: P = W ÷ t, in watts. Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ energy in × 100%. No device is 100% efficient because some energy becomes heat.

Example

A 2 kg book is lifted 1.5 m. What is its gain in PE?

PE = mgh = 2 × 9.8 × 1.5

Answer: 29.4 J

Example

A motor uses 500 J and does 400 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?

400 ÷ 500 × 100%

Answer: 80%

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to square the speed in KE.
  • Thinking energy is lost (it changes to heat).
  • Mixing up power and energy.
